flashcard_questions.q: What is an integrated marketing mix?
flashcard_questions.a: All four elements are linked and support each other with a consistent theme.
An advantage over rivals that attracts more customers and generates more sales.
The rivalry between businesses selling similar products in the same market.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a high price influence the promotion a business chooses?
flashcard_questions.a: It uses premium advertising, such as celebrity endorsements.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a high price influence where a product is sold?
flashcard_questions.a: It goes to exclusive shops such as Harrods.

flashcard_questions.q: How can a low-cost pricing strategy change the product itself?
flashcard_questions.a: Cheaper materials are used to keep costs down.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do products sold online often need more robust packaging?
How does Apple's choice of outlets support its premium image?
flashcard_questions.a: It sells through its own stores and authorised retailers, controlling the experience.

flashcard_questions.q: Why would selling a luxury product in a discount supermarket damage the brand?
flashcard_questions.a: It sends a mixed message about quality.

flashcard_questions.q: Which drinks brand runs the 'Share a Coke' integrated campaign?
What new store format did Iceland launch to reach higher-income earners?
Which rival supermarket lost customers to Iceland's new store format?
What happens to brand awareness when marketing messaging is consistent?
flashcard_questions.a: It increases, because customers see the same brand image everywhere.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens when a business fails to integrate its marketing efforts?
flashcard_questions.a: Inconsistent messaging confuses customers and dilutes brand identity.

flashcard_questions.q: What may a product at the maturity stage need from its marketing mix?
flashcard_questions.a: Refreshed promotion or a price reduction.

notes: 15 cards: 3 term→definition (integrated mix, competitive advantage, competition), 5 knock-on effect cards showing how one P moves another, 4 concept→named example (Apple, Coca-Cola, Iceland Food Warehouse, Farmfoods), 3 single-fact benefit/risk cards. Avoided the 'which P is Place' card — the old deck already asked it.
